user_story: As an operator, I want to know within seconds whether my agent embarrassed me overnight, so that I can stop worrying or start fixing.
expected_behaviour: Leads with a single verdict — a count of things needing action, or an explicit all-clear — before any totals. Volume and cost sit below as context, never as the headline: an agent that hangs up fast would improve 'calls handled' while getting worse.
test_result: pass — verdict reads 'Two things need you' above three ranked items
fix_summary: Job-to-be-done reframe: the page answers 'can I stop worrying', not 'what are my numbers'.

user_story: As an operator scanning quickly, I want severity readable without parsing numbers, so that the worst item finds me rather than me finding it.
expected_behaviour: Each attention row carries a severity stripe as well as wording. Critical and warning are distinguishable without colour alone (stripe position, ordering, and explicit copy).
test_result: pass — 2 critical stripes present and ordered first

user_story: As an operator, I want each failure stated in terms of what callers experienced, so that I can triage by damage rather than by log severity.
expected_behaviour: A broken connector reads '4 callers asked to book and the agent could not' — not 'OAuth token expired'. Impact precedes cause.

user_story: As an operator, I want volume, latency and spend as trends rather than point values, so that I can tell a bad day from a bad direction.
expected_behaviour: Three stat cards, each with a 7-day sparkline, emphasised endpoint, and a stated budget where one exists. Rendered, not decorative.
test_result: pass — 4677 px drawn light and dark

user_story: As an operator, I want the last few calls with their outcome, so that I can spot a pattern the exception list has not yet caught.
expected_behaviour: Newest first, each with duration, outcome, and a severity stripe matching the exception list's vocabulary.

user_story: As an operator with several agents, I want to see which are misbehaving from the list, so that I do not have to open each one to find out.
expected_behaviour: Every row shows status, number, calls today and guardrail adherence. Health is in the list because 'is anything misbehaving' is why the page gets opened; 'last edited' alone would not answer it.
test_result: pass — 3 rows with adherence meters and distinct status chips

user_story: As an operator, I want draft, live and paused to be visually distinct, so that I never edit a live agent believing it is a draft.
expected_behaviour: Three distinct chips. A paused agent shows em-dashes rather than stale numbers, so absence of data does not read as zero traffic.

user_story: As a first-time user, I want my first session to produce a working agent, so that I get value before I lose patience.
expected_behaviour: Empty state is preset cards, never an empty table with a Create button. Each preset is a complete agent — prompt, tools, fixture — that takes a call immediately. Exactly four options; more would trade the first decision for paralysis.

user_story: As a builder, I want to know the generated prompt is a starting point, so that I do not ship a bland draft believing it is finished.
expected_behaviour: Copy states you will rewrite most of it. The product does not claim the draft is production-ready — the observed reviewer rewrote nearly all of theirs.

user_story: As an operator, I want opening an agent to change context clearly, so that I always know whether I am editing one agent or the workspace.
expected_behaviour: Selecting an agent reveals the agent tab strip and the agent's name plus draft state in the header; workspace screens hide both.

user_story: As someone about to give an AI agent access to my company mailbox, I want to know what it can and cannot do before I sign in, so that I can consent rather than gamble.
expected_behaviour: Connect opens a disclosure step first — what it can do, that everything arrives off, and that revoking is immediate — and only then hands off to the provider. Never a bare 'Connect with Google' that jumps straight to consent.
test_result: pass — can/cannot/revoke all present before hand-off
error_detail: Original catalogue design jumped straight to the provider. Handing an autonomous agent OAuth access is the highest-anxiety moment in the product; the anxiety is the design problem, not the click count.
fix_summary: Added a three-step flow with disclosure before hand-off.

user_story: As an operator, I want a newly connected account to grant nothing until I choose, so that connecting is not the same as authorising.
expected_behaviour: On return from the provider every tool is off and the emitted allow-list is an explicit empty array. Saving with nothing enabled is permitted and says so plainly.

user_story: As an operator, I want the allow-list written out even when everything is on, so that a provider adding a tool later cannot silently widen a live agent.
expected_behaviour: allowed_tools is always emitted explicitly and shown to the user. Omission would mean 'all tools', including future ones.
test_result: pass — array updates live and agrees with the switch
error_detail: Both the generic .switch handler and the OAuth handler bound the same elements, so the toggle fired twice: the switch returned to off while the emitted array kept the tool. The security boundary and its control disagreed.
fix_summary: Scoped the generic binding to .switch:not(.oauth-tool); added C11b asserting switch state and allow-list agree.

user_story: As an operator, I want irreversible tools marked, so that I do not enable deletion while skimming a list of five toggles.
expected_behaviour: Destructive tools carry an explicit chip distinct from the accent, in both the workspace connector and the OAuth step.

user_story: As an operator, I want a dead connector to reach me before a customer does, so that I am not silently failing calls for hours.
expected_behaviour: Expiry surfaces in three places: a dashboard exception with caller impact, a nav badge, and a marked card. The connectors page states that tools have been failing mid-call — the consequence, not the status code.
error_detail: First pass had expiry only as a red badge on the connectors page — a page nobody visits until something is already wrong. A refresh token dying is a live production incident, not a settings detail.
fix_summary: Promoted expiry to a dashboard exception with caller impact plus a nav badge.

user_story: As someone who just clicked through to Google, I want the app to show it is waiting, so that I do not think it hung.
expected_behaviour: A distinct waiting step with a live status, a way to re-open the provider window, and a manual 'I've approved it' path for when the callback is missed.

user_story: As a developer whose system is not in the catalogue, I want a custom route, so that an unlisted provider does not block me.
expected_behaviour: Custom MCP server and custom HTTP tool are offered at the top of the catalogue, not buried after eleven logos.

user_story: As a user, I want workspace-level objects separated from agent-level ones, so that I learn the right mental model of what is shared.
expected_behaviour: A persistent workspace rail (Home, Agents, Connectors, Voices, Knowledge, Usage) sits outside the agent tab strip. Shared objects are referenced by agents, never nested inside one.
error_detail: The first mockup had no workspace navigation at all — only an agent tab strip. It taught that connectors and voices live inside an agent, which is the opposite of the IA in the spec and would force re-uploading the same collection per agent.
fix_summary: Added the workspace rail and made the agent chrome context-dependent.

user_story: As a reviewer, I want nav entries with no screen yet to say so, so that I do not read a dead button as a broken product.
expected_behaviour: Voices, Knowledge and Usage open a panel naming why they are in the nav and when the screen lands. No nav item is inert.
error_detail: Nav items initially did nothing when clicked — indistinguishable from a bug.
fix_summary: Added a shared stub screen that names the object and its phase.

user_story: As any user, I want screens to actually hide when navigating, so that I never see two screens stacked.
expected_behaviour: Toggling the hidden attribute reliably hides an element regardless of its class-level display rule.
test_result: pass — mutant with the fix removed fails both
error_detail: Class rules such as .tabs{display:flex} out-specify the UA [hidden] rule, so setting .hidden in JS silently did nothing and the agent tab strip stayed visible on workspace screens.
fix_summary: Added a global [hidden]{display:none !important} with a comment naming the cascade collision.

user_story: As a user on a narrow window, I want no sideways scrolling of the page, so that content is not lost off-screen.
expected_behaviour: Body never scrolls horizontally at 1440 or 390. Wide content scrolls inside its own container. The workspace rail becomes a horizontal strip below 820.

user_story: As a user in dark mode, I want the same care as light mode, so that the product does not feel half-built at night.
expected_behaviour: Tokens redefine under prefers-color-scheme and both data-theme overrides. Canvas graphics re-render on theme change rather than keeping stale colours.

user_story: As a builder, I want the seeded sections to match how people actually write voice prompts, so that I am editing a sensible shape rather than inventing one.
expected_behaviour: Five sections seeded: Identity, Voice & persona, Language, Task flow, Hard rules. Chosen because two independent observed builders converged on that structure; the earlier Greeting/Resolve/Wrap-up default covered only the task flow.
error_detail: Original defaults described only what the agent does, omitting persona, speech style and rules — three of the four things people actually write. Defaults are the highest-leverage control in an authoring UI.

user_story: As a builder, I want a tool mentioned in the prompt to stay correct when I rename the tool, so that my agent does not silently stop calling it mid-call.
expected_behaviour: Tool mentions render as references bound to the tool, not retyped strings. Renaming rewrites every mention; a dangling reference is listed with its section and blocks publish.
test_result: pass — 2 bound refs, 1 broken ref surfaced
error_detail: Observed product requires the user to retype the tool name into the prompt and keep both in sync by hand — stated twice while building. A rename produces a silent production failure with no error anywhere.
fix_summary: Added bound reference tokens plus a tool-reference validation panel.

user_story: As a builder, I want a broken tool reference to reach me before I publish, so that I do not ship an agent that cannot call its own tools.
expected_behaviour: A dangling reference raises the Instructions section to the warning state in the config rail, so it is visible without opening the section.

user_story: As a builder, I want to know when an option makes every call slower, so that I do not trade my latency budget away without noticing.
expected_behaviour: Web search image reading states that it adds latency, at the point of the toggle rather than in documentation.
